correctness.rationale: On every positive weighted path n≥3 the centered Green columns differ by explicit two-level step potentials. Their Gram entries equal min(i,j)(n−max(i,j))/(n w_iw_j), which are strictly positive. Zero column sums give z_v=P_v−Q_v and endpoint columns z_1=−(V_v+Q_v), z_n=P_v+U_v. Left-half indices imply V_v−P_v is a nonnegative combination; right-half indices imply U_v−Q_v is one. Exact squared-norm expansions then show F(v)<F(1) on the left or F(v)<F(n) on the right, for every interior vertex. No infinite assertion rests on the 26,000 finite experiments.

value.rationale: The squared-pseudoinverse diagonal is a mathematically and physically natural local second-order coherence quantity. For every order and heterogeneous weight profile, identifying its exact worst vertex now needs only the two endpoints, with strict exclusion of all interior sites. The all-weight claim is not a trace average or an ordinary first-order resistance identity; its cone proof exploits an exact positive kernel and also yields a squared-biharmonic-distance extremality statement. It is a substantive structural location theorem even without prescribing edge conductances.
